subject: english-literature
source_note: Topic structure follows the Edexcel GCSE English Literature (1ET0) specification. Connections, sequence and prerequisites are expert-authored teaching relationships (exam boards do not publish these).

units.name: Component 1 — Shakespeare & Post-1914 Literature
units.blurb: A Shakespeare play and a post-1914 British play or novel

units.name: Component 2 — 19th-Century Novel & Poetry Since 1789
units.blurb: A 19th-century novel, anthology poetry and unseen poetry

topics.name: Shakespeare
topics.blurb: Close study of a set Shakespeare play, including context

topics.name: Post-1914 British Play or Novel
topics.blurb: A modern British play or novel and its themes

topics.name: 19th-Century Novel
topics.blurb: Close study of a set nineteenth-century novel

topics.name: Poetry Anthology
topics.blurb: Comparing poems from a chosen anthology collection

topics.name: Unseen Poetry
topics.blurb: Comparing two previously unseen contemporary poems

connections.why: Both require analysing drama and prose with their contexts
Skills of close reading and context transfer to the novel
Comparing modern and 19th-century prose sharpens contextual analysis
Anthology comparison builds the skills tested on unseen poems
Themes and language methods recur across prose and poetry
Reading verse drama prepares students for analysing poetry
